🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this upgrade. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ undici (4.15.1 → 7.24.4) · [Repo](https://github.com/nodejs/undici)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Undici has Unbounded Memory Consumption in WebSocket permessage-deflate Decompression

Description

The undici WebSocket client is vulnerable to a denial-of-service attack via unbounded memory consumption during permessage-deflate decompression. When a WebSocket connection negotiates the permessage-deflate extension, the client decompresses incoming compressed frames without enforcing any limit on the decompressed data size. A malicious WebSocket server can send a small compressed frame (a "decompression bomb") that expands to an extremely large size in memory, causing the Node.js process to exhaust available memory and crash or become unresponsive.

The vulnerability exists in the PerMessageDeflate.decompress() method, which accumulates all decompressed chunks in memory and concatenates them into a single Buffer without checking whether the total size exceeds a safe threshold.

Impact

  • Remote denial of service against any Node.js application using undici's WebSocket client
  • A single compressed WebSocket frame of ~6 MB can decompress to ~1 GB or more
  • Memory exhaustion occurs in native/external memory, bypassing V8 heap limits
  • No application-level mitigation is possible as decompression occurs before message delivery

Patches

Users should upgrade to fixed versions.

Workarounds

No workaround are possible.

🚨 Undici has Unbounded Memory Consumption in its DeduplicationHandler via Response Buffering that leads to DoS

Impact

This is an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability (CWE-400) that can lead to Denial of Service (DoS).

In vulnerable Undici versions, when interceptors.deduplicate() is enabled, response data for deduplicated requests could be accumulated in memory for downstream handlers. An attacker-controlled or untrusted upstream endpoint can exploit this with large/chunked responses and concurrent identical requests, causing high memory usage and potential OOM process termination.

Impacted users are applications that use Undici’s deduplication interceptor against endpoints that may produce large or long-lived response bodies.

Patches

The issue has been patched by changing deduplication behavior to stream response chunks to downstream handlers as they arrive (instead of full-body accumulation), and by preventing late deduplication when body streaming has already started.

Users should upgrade to the first official Undici (and Node.js, where applicable) releases that include this patch.

Workarounds

If upgrading immediately is not possible:

  • Disable interceptors.deduplicate() for affected clients/routes.
  • Use skipHeaderNames with a marker header to force high-risk requests to bypass deduplication.
  • Avoid concurrent identical requests to untrusted endpoints that may return very large/chunked bodies.
  • Apply upstream/proxy response-size and timeout limits.

🚨 Undici: Malicious WebSocket 64-bit length overflows parser and crashes the client

Impact

A server can reply with a WebSocket frame using the 64-bit length form and an extremely large length. undici's ByteParser overflows internal math, ends up in an invalid state, and throws a fatal TypeError that terminates the process.

Patches

Patched in the undici version v7.24.0 and v6.24.0. Users should upgrade to this version or later.

Workarounds

There are no workarounds.

🚨 Undici: Malicious WebSocket 64-bit length overflows parser and crashes the client

Impact

A server can reply with a WebSocket frame using the 64-bit length form and an extremely large length. undici's ByteParser overflows internal math, ends up in an invalid state, and throws a fatal TypeError that terminates the process.

Patches

Patched in the undici version v7.24.0 and v6.24.0. Users should upgrade to this version or later.

Workarounds

There are no workarounds.

🚨 Undici has an HTTP Request/Response Smuggling issue

Impact

Undici allows duplicate HTTP Content-Length headers when they are provided in an array with case-variant names (e.g., Content-Length and content-length). This produces malformed HTTP/1.1 requests with multiple conflicting Content-Length values on the wire.

Who is impacted:

  • Applications using undici.request(), undici.Client, or similar low-level APIs with headers passed as flat arrays
  • Applications that accept user-controlled header names without case-normalization

Potential consequences:

  • Denial of Service: Strict HTTP parsers (proxies, servers) will reject requests with duplicate Content-Length headers (400 Bad Request)
  • HTTP Request Smuggling: In deployments where an intermediary and backend interpret duplicate headers inconsistently (e.g., one uses the first value, the other uses the last), this can enable request smuggling attacks leading to ACL bypass, cache poisoning, or credential hijacking

Patches

Patched in the undici version v7.24.0 and v6.24.0. Users should upgrade to this version or later.

body:
Bootstraps the project as a SolidStart + TypeScript SPA with a Claude API integration, local JSON-based conversation history, per-message annotations, and drag-and-drop history loading.

## Agent abstraction
- `src/agents/types.ts` — core interfaces: `AgentAPI`, `AgentConfig`, `Message`, `Conversation`, `AgentResponse`
- `src/agents/claude.ts` — `ClaudeAgent` implementing `AgentAPI` via `@anthropic-ai/sdk`
- `src/agents/index.ts` — `createAgent(config)` factory; extend here to add providers

```typescript
// Adding a new provider is a single case in the factory
export function createAgent(config: AgentConfig): AgentAPI {
  switch (config.provider) {
    case 'claude': return new ClaudeAgent()
    default: throw new Error(`Unknown provider: ${config.provider}`)
  }
}
```

## API routing (key never in client bundle)
- `src/routes/api/chat.ts` — server route receives `{ messages, config }`, calls `createAgent(config).sendMessage(...)`, returns response; API key only travels in the POST body to the server

## Context / history management
- `src/lib/history.ts` — immutable helpers: `createConversation`, `addMessage`, `updateAnnotation`; conversation title auto-set from first user message
- `src/lib/storage.ts` — `saveConversation` (triggers browser JSON download) + `loadConversationFromFile(File)` with schema validation
- Conversation JSON includes optional `annotation` field per message for user notes

## UI
- `ConfigPanel` — provider/model, API key (localStorage, show/hide), system prompt, max tokens
- `Chat` — New / Save / Load actions; conversation metadata kept in sync with config changes via `createEffect`
- `MessageList` — inline annotation add/edit per message
- `MessageInput` — Ctrl/Cmd+Enter to submit
- `DropZone` — modal overlay with drag-and-drop + click-to-browse for importing conversation JSON files
- Plain CSS dark theme with CSS custom properties; responsive (stacks on mobile)

body:
This change introduces a layout-aware PPTX to Markdown conversion pipeline, going beyond simple text extraction. Instead of relying on raw reading order, the implementation leverages geometric (position, size), typographic (font size), and structural heuristics to infer slide semantics such as titles, sections, and content grouping.

This approach is designed to be template-agnostic and deterministic, making it suitable for RAG and ingestion pipelines where consistency and structure are critical. Existing libraries (e.g., python-pptx) provide low-level access but do not offer this level of semantic reconstruction.

The result is significantly improved Markdown quality, especially for multi-column slides and complex layouts, while remaining robust across different presentation styles.

author: viovanov
body:
## PR: Add 6 heavy assault enemy types (Issue #775, Epic #759)

### Summary (what & why)
This PR introduces **six new “heavy assault” enemy variants**—**titan, bastion, siege_engine, colossus, warden, leviathan**—as late-game, mini-boss-tier threats for **late Act 2 and Act 3**. These enemies are **larger, higher-HP, and mechanically distinct** to increase wave variety and require **focused fire + target prioritization**.

Key gameplay mechanics added:
- **Titan**: runtime **weapon switching** (spread ↔ missile) on a timer.
- **Bastion**: **deploys and becomes stationary**, forcing kill-to-progress pressure.
- **Siege Engine**: long-range artillery using **charge_beam**.
- **Colossus**: **directional armor** (top-half hits deal reduced damage).
- **Warden**: **projectile-blocking barrier** with HP + regeneration (also blocks player beam).
- **Leviathan**: **drone spawning** with per-entity cap; kills spawned drones on death.

Additionally, `assignEnemySprite()` is updated to include mappings for the new variants and also fills a **pre-existing mapping gap** for **sentinel → vulture** variants (noted in the spec).

---

### Key files modified
- **`src/games/raptor/types.ts`**
  - Extends `EnemyVariant` union with the 6 new variants
  - Adds entries to `ENEMY_CONFIGS` (stats, weapon types, sizes)
  - Adds corresponding entries to `ENEMY_PROJECTILE_SKINS`

- **`src/games/raptor/entities/Enemy.ts`**
  - Adds per-variant state + movement logic (enter → hold/patrol/drift patterns)
  - Makes `weaponType` mutable to support **titan weapon toggling**
  - Implements **warden barrier state + regen + rendering**
  - Implements **leviathan drone spawn timers/tracking**
  - Adds fallback canvas renderers + HP bar rendering for bastion/colossus/leviathan
  - Adds new variants to the **no-scroll-off cleanup exclusion** list

- **`src/games/raptor/systems/CollisionSystem.ts`**
  - Adds **colossus directional armor** in bullet collision handling
  - Introduces **warden barrier absorption** for player projectiles
  - Extends beam collision to allow **barrier to block player beam hits**

- **`src/games/raptor/RaptorGame.ts`**
  - Adds sprite mappings for the 6 new variants (and fills sentinel–vulture gap)
  - Wires in `checkBarrierAbsorption()` before bullet-enemy collision checks
  - Implements **leviathan drone spawning** during update loop
  - Implements **leviathan death cleanup** (kills any spawned drones)

- **`src/games/raptor/rendering/assets.ts`**
  - Adds sprite manifest entries for:
    - `enemy_titan`, `enemy_bastion`, `enemy_siege_engine`, `enemy_colossus`, `enemy_warden`, `enemy_leviathan`

---

### Testing notes
**Manual verification recommended (gameplay/system-level):**
- Spawn each new variant (debug/spawner) and validate:
  - **Titan** switches weapon type every ~4s and fires with the active type
  - **Bastion** deploys between ~15–35% screen height, becomes stationary, and does not despawn via off-screen cleanup
  - **Siege Engine** holds long-range position and fires `charge_beam`
  - **Colossus** takes reduced damage from top-half bullet hits, full from bottom-half hits
  - **Warden** barrier absorbs player bullets, regenerates over time, and blocks player beam damage to enemies behind it
  - **Leviathan** spawns 2 drones every ~6s up to 6 active; spawned drones die when leviathan dies (no score inflation)

**Regression checks:**
- Ensure existing enemy variants still spawn, move, fire, collide, and render unchanged.
- Confirm sprite assignment works for the newly added variants and that sentinel–vulture mappings are now present in `assignEnemySprite()`.

_No automated test changes were included in this PR; coverage relies on manual playtesting / debug spawns for behavior validation._

author: mango766
body:
The `done` callback in the `writev` handlers of both
`newStreamWritableFromWritableStream` and
`newStreamDuplexFromReadableWritablePair` unconditionally called
`error.filter()`, assuming `error` is always an array (from
`SafePromiseAll`). However, `done` is also used as the rejection
handler for `writer.ready`, which passes a single error value,
not an array. This caused a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of
null (reading 'filter')` which became an unhandled rejection,
crashing the process.

**Root cause:** When a `Duplex.fromWeb()` stream is corked, writes
are batched into a `_writev` call. If `destroy()` is called in the
same microtask (after `uncork()`), the underlying `WritableStream`
writer gets aborted, causing `writer.ready` to reject. The `done`
callback then receives a single error instead of the array it
expects from `SafePromiseAll`.

**Fix:** Check whether `error` is an array before calling
`ArrayPrototypeFilter` on it. This handles both code paths:
- `SafePromiseAll` resolution/rejection → array of results/errors
- `writer.ready` rejection → single error value

Also uses `ArrayIsArray`/`ArrayPrototypeFilter` from primordials,
consistent with Node.js internal conventions.

Includes a regression test that reproduces the exact scenario from
the issue report (cork → write → write → uncork → destroy).

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/62199

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a complete full-stack web application called "Паспорт дома" (Home Passport) - a comprehensive home maintenance and system management platform built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Supabase.

## Key Changes

### Core Application Structure
- **Authentication System**: Login, signup, and password recovery pages with Supabase integration
- **Dashboard Layout**: Responsive sidebar navigation with theme switching (light/dark mode)
- **Demo Mode**: Full application functionality available without authentication for testing

### Main Features Implemented
- **Houses Management**: Create and manage multiple properties with details (address, type, area, year built)
- **Systems Tracking**: Categorize and monitor home systems (heating, water, electrical, etc.) with maintenance schedules
- **Maintenance Logs**: Record maintenance, repairs, inspections, and replacements with costs and master assignments
- **Reminders System**: Smart reminder categorization (overdue, today, soon, this month, later) for upcoming maintenance
- **Masters Directory**: Manage contractor/specialist contacts with specialization and phone information
- **Expenses Tracking**: Log and filter expenses by house, system, and time period with analytics
- **Documents Management**: Store and organize documents (receipts, warranties, manuals, photos, contracts) with file size tracking
- **Settings & Sharing**: User account management, password changes, and house member invitations with role-based access

author: 13otkmdr
body:
💡 What: The O(N*K) slice calculations for `upper_channel`, `lower_channel`, `short_stop`, and `long_stop` inside `TurtleTradingChannel`'s main loop have been extracted and vectorized using `pandas.Series.rolling(window=period).max()` and `.min()`.

🎯 Why: The original implementation iterated over all elements and computed the max/min of an array slice in each iteration (`np.max(high[start_idx:i + 1])`). For an input array of size N and period K, this operates in O(N*K) time, causing a significant performance bottleneck. By using Pandas rolling, the complexity is reduced to O(N).

📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement is ~13.5x speedup (measured drop from 2.23s to 0.16s for 100k data points).

🔬 Measurement: Run performance benchmarks generating a 100k element random array and timing the `.calculate` execution time of the `TurtleTradingChannel` indicator. Run unit tests (`pytest tests/test_indicators_baseline.py`) to verify results remain exactly identical, including NaN handling for the initial periods.

author: 1abhishekpandey
body:
## Description
The PR validation pipeline relied on fragile shell scripts for module discovery, quality checks, and artifact builds. These scripts used manual `find`/`grep` patterns to locate Gradle modules and ran quality tasks through bespoke wrappers, making the CI brittle and difficult to maintain. Additionally, all jobs ran on GitHub-hosted runners, and PRs targeting `main` were never validated because the workflow's branch filter was missing `main`.

This umbrella PR consolidates four targeted fixes that modernise the CI pipeline:

1. **Gradle-native module discovery** - Replaced shell-based module discovery with a `listModules` Gradle task that outputs `all_modules`, `android_modules`, and `jvm_modules`. Quality check actions now use a shared `run-gradle-tasks.sh` script instead of individual wrappers. Gradle build cache (`gradle/actions/setup-gradle`) added to all check actions.

2. **Stale CI cleanup** - Removed five files (`build-aars/action.yml`, `setup-and-validate/action.yml`, `build-aars.sh`, `find-affected-modules.sh`, `run-quality-checks.sh`) that were superseded by the module discovery refactor.

3. **Self-hosted runners** - Switched all PR validation jobs from `ubuntu-latest` to `[self-hosted, Linux, X64]` and added an Android SDK setup script for environments that don't have Android tooling pre-installed.

4. **Branch filter fix** - Added `main` to the PR validation workflow's `branches` filter so that PRs targeting `main` (e.g. release merges, hotfixes) are now validated.

## Type of change
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [x] Code refactor/optimization

## Implementation Details
- Replaced `setup-and-find-modules` action with `setup-and-list-modules` that uses the Gradle `listModules` task for reliable, Gradle-native module enumeration
- Created `scripts/run-gradle-tasks.sh` as a shared runner that iterates over a module list and executes a given Gradle task, replacing per-action shell logic
- Refactored `build-check`, `detekt-check`, `lint-check`, and `test-check` actions to accept module lists as inputs and delegate to the shared script
- Added `gradle/actions/setup-gradle` with `cache-read-only: true` to all check actions for faster CI builds
- Updated `pr-validation.yml` to run the build job in parallel with quality checks and restructured job dependencies
- Switched all workflow jobs from `ubuntu-latest` to `[self-hosted, Linux, X64]`
- Added `scripts/setup-android-sdk.sh` to install Android SDK components on self-hosted runners that lack pre-installed Android tooling
- Added `main` to the `pull_request.branches` filter in `pr-validation.yml`
- Deleted five stale files that were no longer referenced by any workflow

## Checklist
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.
- [ ] I have added the necessary documentation (if appropriate).
- [x] I have ensured that my code follows the project's code style.
- [ ] I have checked for potential performance impacts and optimized if necessary.
- [ ] I have checked the code for security issues.
- [ ] I have updated the changelog (if required).

## How to test?
1. Raise a draft PR targeting `develop` and confirm the PR Validation workflow triggers, discovers modules via the Gradle task, and all quality check jobs pass on self-hosted runners.
2. Raise a draft PR targeting `main` and confirm the workflow triggers (previously it did not).
3. Verify that the build job runs in parallel with quality checks rather than sequentially.
4. Confirm no references remain to the deleted files (`build-aars`, `setup-and-validate`, `find-affected-modules.sh`, `run-quality-checks.sh`, `build-aars.sh`).

## Breaking Changes
None.

## Maintainers Checklist
- [ ] The code has been reviewed.
- [ ] CI tests have passed.
- [ ] All necessary documentation has been updated.

## Screenshots (if applicable)
N/A

## Additional Context
This is an umbrella PR combining four sub-issue PRs (#283, #285, #286, #288) that were individually reviewed and merged into this branch.

# Summary

<!-- 
  Be sure your Pull Request includes:

  - JIRA ticket number in the title, and link in the summary
  - An accurate summary of what is being added/edited/removed
  - Tests (unit, component, regression)
  - Updated documentation and commented code
  - Link to Figma, if applicable
  - Conventional Commits
-->

This PR adds a `codeRenderer` function prop to `KCodeBlock` for flicker-free syntax highlighting.

Previously, applying syntax highlighting required listening to `@code-block-render` and mutating `codeElement.innerHTML` which causes a flash of unstyled code:


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d7501cd-e334-4fed-bc35-f20c3eac1d9f


With `codeRenderer`, the component awaits the returned HTML internally before rendering, so unstyled code is never visible. On subsequent updates, the previous highlighted content stays visible until the new result arrives. This also helps eliminate flaky tests caused by syntax highlighters in consumer apps. Previously, tests could observe the un-highlighted code before the highlighter replaced it.

🛡️ Sentinel: [HIGH] Fix timing attack vulnerability in cron endpoint

🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: Authorization check in retention-notifications cron uses strict equality operator (`===`), allowing for timing attacks to guess the secret.
🎯 Impact: Attackers can potentially brute-force the CRON_SECRET character-by-character, allowing unauthorized execution of cron tasks.
🔧 Fix: Created a `safeCompare` utility in `@/lib/security` using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` with SHA-256 hashes, and updated the cron endpoint to use it.

author: copilot
body:
Three compounding gaps prevented `wwwroot/App_Plugins` content (backoffice JS bundles, `paste-from-word.min.js`, `umbraco-package.json`) from reaching consuming projects:

1. **Never built in CI** — `npm run backoffice` (the Vite build for both `Backoffice/` directories) was never called in `azure-pipelines.yml`, so `wwwroot/App_Plugins/` was never generated (it's `.gitignore`d)
2. **Not in NuGet packages** — because the files didn't exist at build time, they weren't picked up as static web assets
3. **Not copied to consumers** — the `.targets` files copied CSS and uSync but had no logic for `App_Plugins`

## Changes

### `Directory.Build.targets` (both Umbraco projects)
Added a `BuildTypeScript` MSBuild target chained `AfterTargets` the existing version-file-generation step. Runs `npm install` (conditional on `node_modules` absence) then `npm run build`, so the Vite output exists before the NuGet package is assembled:

```xml
<Target Name="GovUkFrontendUmbraco_BuildTypeScript" AfterTargets="GovUkFrontendUmbraco_GenerateTypeScriptVersion">
    <Exec Command="npm install"
          WorkingDirectory="$(MsBuildThisFileDirectory)Backoffice"
          Condition="!Exists('$(MsBuildThisFileDirectory)Backoffice\node_modules')" />
    <Exec Command="npm run build"
          WorkingDirectory="$(MsBuildThisFileDirectory)Backoffice" />
</Target>
```

### `*.targets` (both Umbraco packages)
Added an `App_Plugins` source path (`staticwebassets\App_Plugins\<PackageName>\`) and a `Copy` task to deposit files into the consuming project's `wwwroot\App_Plugins\<PackageName>\`, plus `.gitignore` generation to prevent accidental commits — consistent with the existing CSS/uSync patterns.

### `azure-pipelines.yml`
Added `Cache@2` + conditional `npm ci` steps for both Backoffice `node_modules` directories, placed before the dotnet build steps. Pre-installing dependencies means the MSBuild `npm install` condition is false in CI and only `npm run build` runs during the dotnet build.

author: timwkosatec
body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #16882

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

PR #14707 added auto-compaction recovery for 413/context overflow errors, but the `ContextOverflowError` catch block in `processor.ts` unconditionally sets `needsCompaction = true` without checking the `compaction.auto` config. Users who set `compaction: { "auto": false }` still get forced into a compaction loop on overflow, and switching to a model with a larger context window doesn't recover the session.

This adds a `config.compaction?.auto === false` gate to the overflow catch path:

- **auto: false** — treats the overflow as a normal error: persists it on the assistant message, publishes the error event, sets the session to idle, and returns `"stop"`. The user can then resume with a different model.
- **auto: true / undefined (default)** — keeps the existing behavior from #14707 (`needsCompaction = true` → compact and recover).

The strict `=== false` check means the default (`undefined`) still compacts, so this is backward-compatible. Manual compaction (`/compact`) remains available regardless of the `auto` setting.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added two tests in `compaction.test.ts`:

1. `stops on provider overflow when compaction.auto is false` — verifies result is `"stop"`, error is persisted as `ContextOverflowError`, no compaction parts written.
2. `compacts on provider overflow when compaction.auto is true` — verifies result is `"compact"`, no error on assistant message.

Run with:
```
cd packages/opencode && bun test test/session/compaction.test.ts
cd packages/opencode && bun typecheck
```

Also verified no regressions in:
- `bun test test/session/retry.test.ts` (18 pass)
- `bun test test/session/message-v2.test.ts -t "fromError"` (6 pass)

author: rob23oba
body: This PR fixes a segfault when running `idbgClientLoop`. `@[extern]` expects that the function doesn't include erased arguments in the signature; however, `@[export]` exports the function with all arguments, including erased ones. This causes a function signature mismatch between `idbgClientLoopImpl` and `idbgClientLoop`, causing segfaults. However, instead of solving the deeper problem that `@[extern]` - `@[export]` pairs can cause such problems, this PR removes the erased arguments from `idbgClientLoopImpl` and replaces occurrences of `α` with `NonScalar`.

- **Removed hardcoded JWT secret fallback** — the default string `wristnerd-admin-default-secret-change-me` was publicly visible in source code, allowing anyone to forge admin tokens
- **Removed hardcoded demo credentials** — `admin123`, `editor123`, `viewer123` were committed to the public repo
- **Removed master password backdoor** — `NEXT_PUBLIC_ADMIN_MASTER_PASSWORD` bypass eliminated
- **Added runtime warnings** when required auth env vars are not configured
- **Added proper error** when `JWT_SECRET_KEY` is missing and token signing/verification is attempted

#### XSS Prevention
- **Enabled HTML sanitization in remark-html** (markdown.ts) — was `sanitize: false`, allowing arbitrary script injection
- **Sanitized JSON-LD schema markup** (SchemaMarkup.tsx) — now parses and re-serializes JSON to strip non-JSON content

#### Security Headers (_headers)
- Added `Strict-Transport-Security` (HSTS) with 1-year max-age, includeSubDomains, and preload
- Added `X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block`
- Added `Content-Security-Policy` restricting script, style, font, image, and connect sources
- Added `Cache-Control` headers for static assets (immutable) and HTML pages (must-revalidate)

#### Crawler Protection
- Created `robots.txt` blocking `/admin/` and `/login` from search engine crawlers

#### Dependency Cleanup
- Removed unused `@next/font` and `next-mdx-remote` dependencies

---

### Commit 2: Bug Fixes & Optimizations

#### EmailSignup Fix
- Removed broken `fetch("/api/subscribe")` call (endpoint does not exist in static export)
- Added client-side email validation and honeypot bot detection
- Added TODO comment for future subscription endpoint integration

#### MarkdownEditor XSS Fix
- Added HTML escaping before applying markdown regex formatting in admin preview
- Prevents script injection via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`

#### Gift Finder Fixes
- Fixed **Citizen Eco-Drive Chandler** linking to wrong review page (was `/reviews/citizen-eco-drive-bm8180`, now `/reviews/citizen-eco-drive-chandler`)
- Replaced all placeholder `#` affiliate links with real Amazon URLs with `wristnerd-20` tag (was losing affiliate revenue)

#### SEO & Sitemap Fixes
- Fixed sitemap `lastModified` using `new Date()` on every build — now uses fixed `BUILD_DATE` so crawlers are not misled into thinking all content is new
- Added `/admin/` and `/login` to `robots.ts` disallow list
- Added `noindex`/`nofollow` meta to admin layout to prevent search engine indexing

---

Set these environment variables in your Cloudflare Pages deployment:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_JWT_SECRET=<generate-a-strong-random-secret>
NEXT_PUBLIC_ADMIN_EMAIL=<your-admin-email>
NEXT_PUBLIC_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<strong-password>
```

author: simonepri
body:
## Problem

The readme update step in the release job checks out the release PR branch (`git checkout "$BRANCH"`) to amend the version pin, but never switches back to `main`. The subsequent `release-plz release` command then runs on the PR branch — which has the bumped version in `Cargo.toml` — and creates a release before the PR is merged.

This creates an infinite cycle: each merged release PR triggers a premature release of the *next* version, which spawns another release PR, and so on (v0.5.1 → v0.5.2 → v0.5.3 with no actual changes).

## Solution

Re-checkout `main` (with full history) before the `release` step so it only releases versions that have actually been merged.

## Cleanup needed

After merging, manually delete the ghost release v0.5.3 and its tag, and close PR #7.

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/kang49/bilibili-story-sharing/security/code-scanning/5](https://github.com/kang49/bilibili-story-sharing/security/code-scanning/5)

General approach: Ensure that *every* URL used in outgoing HTTP requests is restricted to allowed schemes and hosts, including URLs obtained via redirects. Introduce a small helper to validate URLs, and apply it both to the initial input and to any redirect URLs before using them. If the redirect does not meet the constraints, abort instead of following/using it. Also, guard against missing `responseUrl` to avoid runtime errors.

Best concrete fix for this code:

- Keep `regenerate_path`’s logic but refactor the validation into a reusable helper, e.g. `isAllowedBilibiliUrl(url: URL): boolean`, so we can apply the same checks to `redirectedLink`.
- In `findName`, after `axios.get(biliLink)` and before using `initialResponse.request.res.responseUrl`, parse that redirect URL into a `URL` object and validate:
  - Scheme must be `https:`.
  - Hostname must be exactly `www.bilibili.tv`.
- If the redirect is missing or invalid, throw or return an error instead of proceeding.
- Optionally, disable further redirects on the *second* set of requests (`fetchPageName`) to ensure we only ever follow the one redirect we explicitly validated.

Where and what to change:

1. In `src/findAnimeName.ts`:
   - Above `regenerate_path`, add a small helper `function isAllowedBilibiliUrl(parsed: URL): boolean` that enforces the `https` + `www.bilibili.tv` constraint.
   - Update `regenerate_path` to use this helper instead of duplicating the checks.
   - In `findName`:
     - After `const initialResponse = await axios.get(biliLink);`, obtain `redirectedLink` more defensively, e.g. `(initialResponse.request?.res?.responseUrl as string) || biliLink`.
     - Parse `redirectedLink` using `new URL(redirectedLink)` and validate with `isAllowedBilibiliUrl`. If invalid, throw an error.
     - Optionally, pass `{ maxRedirects: 0 }` to `axios.get` calls inside `fetchPageName` so that we don’t silently follow any further redirects without validation.

These changes preserve existing functionality (still following Bilibili redirects and deriving `/en/` and `/th/` URLs) while ensuring every outgoing URL is constrained to the allowed host and scheme, thus addressing all three CodeQL variants that stem from user-controlled input.

## New files

- **`Models/ShelvingRow.cs`** — Output model matching ExtractTest's schema
- **`Models/ShelvingRowMap.cs`** — CsvHelper column mapping
- **`Utils/Parsing.cs`** — `ToIntOrNull`, `ToDecimalOrNull`, `ParseShelvesFromText`, plus new `ParseMaxLoadFromText` (matches `(\d+)\s*kg\s*(per shelf|per level|UDL)`)
- **`Utils/DimensionsParsing.cs`** — Ported from ExtractTest with regex bug fixed (`s*` → `\s*` in `SingleLabelRegex`)
- **`CompleteScraper.cs`** — Combined extraction logic (see below)

## Modified files

- **`TuffermanScraper.Complete.csproj`** — Added `HtmlAgilityPack` + `CsvHelper`, pinned to `net8.0`
- **`Program.cs`** — Wired up `CompleteScraper`, 4 test URLs, writes `Tufferman-Complete-Shelving.csv`

## Extraction logic decisions

| Field | Source |
|---|---|
| Prices (ex-VAT) | HTML `price-list ex-vat` block first; fallback to JSON inc-VAT ÷ 1.2 |
| Width / Depth | `option1` / `option2`; if not clean integers, split variant title `"W / D / Load"` |
| Max load | `option3` first; fallback `ParseMaxLoadFromText` on description |
| Number of shelves | HTML levels metafield; fallback `ParseShelvesFromText` regex |
| Upright colour | HTML metafield colour swatch; fallback keyword scan on title/description |
| Assembly | Enhanced: boltless, bolt-free, no nuts/bolts, flat packed + assembly, comes assembled |
| Finish | Enhanced: powder-coated (hyphenated), stainless steel, chrome catch-all |
| Range | Fixed pre-existing typo `"Shlving with Boxes"` → `"Shelving with Boxes"` |

Shopify JSON is parsed via `JsonDocument` manual field extraction to avoid `JsonSerializer` crashes on unmapped properties.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Overview

Create the completed scraper in the `TuffermanScraper.Complete` project by combining the best working extraction logic from the two existing projects (`TuffermanScraper.Test` and `TuffermanScraper.ExtractTest`). The `TuffermanScraper.Complete` project already exists with a bare `Program.cs` and `.csproj` — it needs to be fully built out.

## Column-to-source mapping

Based on the user's testing, here is which project's logic works best for each CSV column:

### From `TuffermanScraper.Test` (the `TuffermanScraper/TuffermanProductExtractor.cs` file):
- **Range** — `DetectRange()` with predefined `AllRanges` list + fuzzy fallbacks (but fix the typo `"Shlving with Boxes"` → `"Shelving with Boxes"`)
- **Height** — `DetectHeightFromTitle()` + `DetectHeightFromUrl()` fallback
- **Width** — From variant `option1` (parsed as int)
- **Depth** — From variant `option2` (parsed as int)
- **Shelf Type** — `DetectShelfType()` from description text (MDF, melamine, wire mesh, etc.)
- **Assembly** — `DetectAssembly()` but enhanced with ExtractTest's more thorough checks (boltless, bolt-free, bolt free, self assembly, self-assembly, no nuts and bolts, no nuts, no bolts, flat packed + assembly, fully assembled, comes assembled)
- **Supplier** — `product.Vendor` from the Shopify JSON
- **Add-on bay?** — `DetectIsAddOnBay()` from title + description (extension bay, add-on bay, add on bay)
- **Location** — The product page URL
- **Bullets** — `ExtractDescriptionText()` that flattens all text nodes from `DescriptionHtml` with `" | "` separators
- **Comments** — Empty string

### From `TuffermanScraper.ExtractTest`:
- **Number of Shelves** — First try `ExtractLevelsForVariant()` from HTML metafields, then fallback to `Parsing.ParseShelvesFromText()` regex (`\b(\d+)\s*(adjustable\s+)?(levels?|shelves?|shelf)\b`)
- **Component** — From `ShelvingRowTransformer`: if text contains "extension bay"/"add-on bay"/"add on bay" → `"Add-on bay"`, if "starter bay" → `"Starter bay"`, else null
- **Warranty** — From `ShelvingRowTransformer`: if supplier is "Storalex" → 5 years, else scan text for number before "year", default to 1
- **Delivery** — `ExtractDeliveryDays()` from product indicators div + delivery tab (looks for "24hr", "24 hr", "next day")

### New/combined logic:
- **Max Load Per Level** — First try parsing from variant `option3` (strip non-digits from strings like `"200kg"`). If that's null, scan the description text for patterns like: `"(\d+)\s*kg\s*(per\s+shelf|per\s+level|UDL)"`. This addresses the user's note to look for "kg per shelf" and "UDL" keywords.
- **Was / Now prices (EX VAT)** — Use ExtractTest's `ExtractPricesExVat()` which reads EX VAT prices directly from the HTML (`price-list` + `ex-vat` CSS classes). This is proven to work. Fall back: if the HTML EX-VAT block isn't found, convert the Shopify JSON inc-VAT prices by dividing by 1.2 (standard UK VAT). The `ExtractPricesExVat` method finds: `.//span[contains(@class,'price--compare')]//span[contains(@class,'price-js')]` for Was, and `.//span[contains(@class,'price--highlight')]//span[contains(@class,'price-js')]` for Now.
- **Upright Colour** — First try ExtractTest's `ExtractColourMetafieldValue()` from HTML metafields, then fallback to Test's `DetectColourFromTitleOrDescription()` (grey/gray, blue, black, white)
- **Finish** — Enhanced: powder coated, powder-coated, epoxy, galvanised/galvanized, stainless steel, nickel chrome, chrome shelving

## JSON parsing approach

The Shopify product JSON is in `<script type="application/json" data-product-json>`. Use `JsonDocument` manual parsing (NOT `JsonSerializer.Deserialize` with model classes) to avoid crashes from unmapped properties. Only extract the fields we actually need:
- `product.id`, `product.title`, `product.vendor`, `product.description`
- `product.variants[]` — for each: `id`, `title`, `option1`, `option2`, `option3`, `price`, `compare_at_price`

The `price` and `compare_at_price` from JSON are INC VAT — they should only be used as a fallback (divided by 1.2) if the HTML EX VAT extraction fails.

## Variant dimension parsing

For width/depth/load from each variant, try this priority:
1. Parse from variant's `option1` (width), `option2` (depth), `option3` (load) — these are usually clean values like `"900"`, `"450"`, `"200kg"`
2. If option1 doesn't parse as a clean integer (e.g. it contains concatenated dimensions like `"1800900450"`), try parsing the variant's `title` field which has format `"900 / 450 / 200kg"` — split on `" / "` and extract width, depth, load

All files go under `TuffermanScraper.Complete/`:

1. **`TuffermanScraper.Complete.csproj`** — Update to add `HtmlAgilityPack` and `CsvHelper` NuGet packages
2. **`Models/ShelvingRow.cs`** — The output row model (same schema as ExtractTest's `ShelvingRow`)

## Bug
https://github.com/cloudreve/cloudreve/issues/3369 — Cursor pagination causes frontend errors with "Invalid cloudreve uri" while traditional pagination works correctly.

## Root Cause
The cursor pagination was failing due to inconsistent query selection logic in the  function. The previous implementation had overlapping conditions that could lead to incorrect query selection, particularly when  was true but other query type flags were also set.

## Fix
Reorganized the query selection logic to be mutually exclusive and properly prioritized:

1. **Mixed type queries** take precedence ()
2. **Folder-only queries** are handled next () 
3. **File-only queries** are handled when folders are exhausted ()
4. **Default case** maintains original behavior for normal pagination

## Testing
This fix ensures:
- Consistent query selection regardless of token state
- Proper handling of edge cases in cursor pagination
- No regression in traditional pagination behavior
- Frontend receives well-formed pagination responses

The solution maintains backward compatibility while fixing the logical inconsistency that caused malformed responses.

author: xtline
body:
## Summary

This PR tightens `pulsar-lite` Shared subscription behavior in four areas:

- fix Shared flow permit ordering to avoid dispatch races
- fix Shared ack ownership / recovery handling for non-partitioned message ids
- expand high-level Shared integration coverage using the official Python client
- refresh the Shared difference notes to reflect the current implementation and remaining gaps

## Background

While validating Shared subscription behavior against native Pulsar semantics, two classes of issues showed up:

1. Shared flow dispatch could race with consumer-local permit updates, which made dispatch observe aggregate permits before the selected consumer had visible local permits.
2. Shared ack / recovery could mis-handle non-partitioned message ids, because broker/storage used `partition = -1` internally while the ack parsing path defaulted missing partition values incorrectly, which could lead to ownership mismatches and replay of already-acked messages during recovery.

## What changed

### 1. Shared flow ordering
Adjusted the Shared flow path so consumer-local permits are updated before the dispatcher is triggered, which aligns more closely with native Pulsar's ordering and avoids the "dispatcher sees permits but no consumer is selectable" race.

### 2. Shared ack ownership and recovery
Updated Shared ack handling to keep protocol-level non-partitioned message ids aligned with broker/storage representation and continue matching ownership using the full `MessageId`.

Also tightened consumer removal / recovery by closing pending-ack tracking before draining pending messages for replay.

### 3. Test coverage
Expanded high-level Shared integration coverage in `tests/` using the official Python client:

- Shared round-robin / dispatcher behavior
- Shared flow-control behavior with small `receiver_queue_size`
- pending ack redelivery after consumer close
- already-acked messages are not replayed after owner close
- recovery does not replay already-acked messages
- Java coverage for Shared consumer priority remains separate

### 4. Documentation
Updated `docs/difference/shared_subscription_comparison.md` to reflect:
- the native Pulsar timing model used for comparison
- the Shared ack / recovery bug that was fixed
- the current remaining storage-level gaps

## Key files

- `rust/src/broker/handler/consumer_handler.rs`
- `rust/src/broker/service/consumer.rs`
- `rust/src/broker/dispatcher/shared.rs`
- `tests/test_shared_dispatcher.py`
- `tests/test_shared_flow_control.py`
- `tests/test_shared_integration.py`
- `docs/difference/shared_subscription_comparison.md`

## Validation

Run:

```bash
cargo test -q
pytest tests/test_shared_simple.py tests/test_shared_dispatcher.py tests/test_shared_flow_control.py tests/test_shared_integration.py -q
```
## Notes / remaining gaps
This PR is intentionally scoped to Shared mode only.

It does not attempt to change Exclusive / Failover behavior.

There is still a structural gap in storage modeling: Shared assignment / ack tracking is still relatively coarse compared to native Pulsar, especially around full replay-controller semantics and richer unacked-message management and The mistake regarding consumer priority has **not yet been addressed**.

This pull request introduces the core implementation for the customer checkout and order management features in the client-facing API. It adds controllers, DTOs, services, and mappers to support placing orders, applying vouchers, viewing order history and details, and handling order actions like cancel and reorder. The changes are grouped into three main themes: controller endpoints, service logic, and data transfer objects/mapping.

**Controller Endpoints:**

* Added `CheckoutController` to handle checkout form display, voucher calculation via AJAX, and order confirmation for customers (`/checkout`).
* Added `OrderClientController` to allow customers to list their orders, view order details, cancel orders, and reorder cancelled orders (`/orders`).

**Service Logic:**

* Implemented `CheckoutClientService` to handle cart validation, voucher calculation, and order placement, including updating customer info, voucher usage, and clearing the cart after order placement.

**Data Transfer Objects and Mapping:**

* Introduced request and response DTOs for order creation (`OrderCreateRequest`), checkout summary (`CheckoutSummaryResponse`), order list (`OrderListClientResponse`), and order detail (`OrderDetailResponse` with nested item/history classes). Workers persist state to disk (`tasks//`) with heartbeat, control, and output files. - **Task control tools**: `TaskList`, `TaskOutput`, `TaskStop` give the LLM a generic control plane for background tasks (read-only enumeration, output inspection with blocking/non-blocking modes, graceful stop). - **Notification infrastructure**: Decouple notifications from background tasks into a standalone, producer-agnostic system (`notifications/`). Each notification is a persisted event with per-sink (llm, wire, shell) delivery tracking (pending → claimed → acked). Background task completion is just one notification type. - **LLM sink**: `KimiSoul._step()` delivers pending notifications as independent `` messages in context, with task output tail. Notification messages are excluded from `normalize_history()` merging. - **Wire sink**: `run_soul()` pumps notifications to wire via a periodic background task. Late-published notifications are flushed in the `finally` block. - **Shell sink**: `NotificationWatcher` polls and toasts in the idle shell. The `/task` slash command opens an interactive TUI browser. - **Compaction recovery**: After context compaction, active background tasks are re-injected as an `` snapshot. - **Exit cleanup**: By default, all active background tasks are killed on CLI exit. Configurable via `background.keep_alive_on_exit = true`. - **Print UI**: Notifications arriving mid-stream are buffered until a safe message boundary to avoid splitting assistant messages. ## Test plan - [x] `tests/background/` — store, manager, worker (heartbeat, kill, timeout, recovery, notification publishing) - [x] `tests/notifications/` — manager (dedupe, claim/ack, recovery, deliver_pending) - [x] `tests/core/test_notifications.py` — KimiSoul notification injection, wire pump, compaction snapshot - [x] `tests/tools/test_background_tools.py` — Shell background mode, TaskOutput, TaskList, TaskStop - [x] `tests/ui_and_conv/` — live view notifications, print notifications, task browser, shell slash, prompt history, replay - [x] `tests_e2e/test_wire_sessions.py` — wire protocol e2e - [x] `make check` — ruff + pyright pass (0 errors in src) ---

author: ll1r1k-1337
body:
💡 **What**: Refactored `readTokenAt` in `src/binary/reader.ts` to speculatively read 16 bytes in a single asynchronous `readBytes` call, instead of reading a single byte to check the type and conditionally making subsequent asynchronous reads for payload lengths/values.
🎯 **Why**: When reading binary format tokens, sequential microtasks (such as an `await` for a 1-byte token followed by an `await` for its 4-byte payload) significantly hinder the event loop and degrade throughput. Reading 16 bytes eagerly can resolve the majority of smaller tokens entirely in memory synchronously without any further `await` calls.
📊 **Impact**: Reduces asynchronous I/O read operations in `readTokenAt` significantly. Benchmarks showed token read throughput increased by roughly 17% (from ~600,000 to ~700,000 tokens/s).
🔬 **Measurement**: Verify with `npx tsx benchmarks/bench-read.ts` which measures sequential token read speeds. Tests can be run with `npm run test`.

author: teknium1
body:
## Summary

Salvage of PR #1471 by @peteromallet — thread safety fixes for concurrent subagent delegation.

### The problem

Running 3+ subagents concurrently via `delegate_task` in batch mode causes segfaults, data corruption, and intermittent crashes from four distinct race conditions.

### Fixes

**1. Remove `redirect_stdout`/`redirect_stderr` from delegate_tool**
`contextlib.redirect_stdout` mutates the global `sys.stdout`. When multiple child agents start concurrently in a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, the race between redirect and the spinner thread corrupts the file descriptor, causing segfaults. The redirect was redundant — children already run with `quiet_mode=True`.

**2. Split agent construction from execution**
`_run_single_child()` → `_build_child_agent()` (main thread, serial) + `_run_single_child()` (worker thread, parallel). `AIAgent` construction creates httpx clients and initializes SSL contexts, which are not thread-safe to do concurrently.

**3. Add `threading.Lock` to `SessionDB`**
Subagents share the parent's `SessionDB` and call `create_session()`, `append_message()`, etc. from worker threads with no synchronization. Every database-accessing method is now wrapped in `with self._lock:`.

**4. Add `_active_children_lock` to `AIAgent`**
`interrupt()` iterates `_active_children` while worker threads append/remove children. Now copies the list under lock before iterating.

**5. Add `_client_cache_lock` to `auxiliary_client`**
Multiple subagent threads may resolve auxiliary clients concurrently via `call_llm()`. Double-checked locking pattern prevents duplicate client creation.

### What was NOT included from the original PR

- Per-task `model`/`provider` overrides in `delegate_task` schema (feature addition, not a safety fix)
- `resolve_provider_credentials()` helper (utility, not needed for the safety fixes)
- `_apply_provider_credentials()` extraction in `run_agent.py` (refactoring, not a safety fix)

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `tools/delegate_tool.py` | Split build/run, remove redirect, use lock |
| `hermes_state.py` | Add `threading.Lock` to all DB methods |
| `run_agent.py` | Add `_active_children_lock`, use in `interrupt()` |
| `agent/auxiliary_client.py` | Add `_client_cache_lock`, double-checked locking |
| 6 test files | Update for new `_run_single_child` signature + add `_active_children_lock` |

### Tests

Full suite: 4911 passed, 8 pre-existing failures (unrelated), 200 skipped.

## Credit

Original implementation by @peteromallet (PR #1471).
Closes #1471

body:
Code review pass over the profasta library addressing correctness issues, misleading APIs, inaccurate documentation, and a memory inefficiency.

## `parser.py`
- **`@classmethod` signatures**: `AbstractHeaderParser.parse` and `AbstractHeaderWriter.write` Protocol stubs used `self` instead of `cls`
- **Parameter naming**: `register_writer(name, parser)` and `get_writer(parser_name)` used `parser`/`parser_name` — renamed to `writer`/`writer_name`
- **Module docstring**: `UniprotWriter` and `UniprotLikeWriter` were listed as `"Parser for …"` — corrected to `"Writer for …"`
- **`DefaultParser` docstring**: claimed `header_fields["description"]` "might be an empty string"; the key is actually **absent** when there is no description

## `io.py`
- **Memory inefficiency**: `parse_fasta` called `file_object.read()` upfront, loading the entire file before yielding anything — replaced with a line-by-line streaming implementation:

```python
# Before — reads whole file into memory despite being a generator
fasta_text = file_object.read()
for block in fasta_text.split("\n>")[1:]:
    ...
    yield FastaRecord(header, sequence)

# After — true streaming
for line in file_object:
    if line.startswith(">"):
        if header is not None:
            yield FastaRecord(header, "".join(sequence_lines)...)
        header = line[1:].strip()
        sequence_lines = []
    else:
        sequence_lines.append(line.rstrip("\n"))
```
- **Module docstring**: `parse_fasta` described as "return a list" — corrected to "yield"

## `db.py`
- **Missing type annotation**: `write_fasta`'s `path` parameter was untyped — added `str`
- **Loose type annotation**: `skipped_fasta_entries: dict[str, list]` → `dict[str, list[str]]`
- **Incomplete warning**: `add_fasta` warning ended with a dangling colon and never printed the skipped headers — now includes them in the log message

## `tests/integration/test_integration.py`
- `CustomWriter.write` `@classmethod` stub used `self` instead of `cls`

author: arhtudormorar
body:
### Issue

Account balance does not update in the UI after receiving an incoming transaction via WebSocket.

### Reproduce

Issue exists on sdk-dapp v5 (Zustand store).

1. Log in to dapp with any account
2. Have a second account send EGLD to the logged-in account
3. Observe that the `transactionCompleted` WebSocket event fires and the `TransactionReceivedToast` appears — but the account balance displayed on the dashboard remains stale

### Root cause

`trackTransactions` → `recheckStatus` → `checkTransactionStatus` exits early when there are no pending outgoing transaction sessions (`entries.length === 0`). This is always the case for incoming transactions since the wallet has no session tracking them.

For outgoing transactions, `checkBatch` calls `refreshAccount()` once the batch completes, which updates the Zustand account store. For incoming transactions, nothing triggered `refreshAccount()`, leaving the balance stale until a page refresh.

In sdk-dapp v4 (Redux-based) this was handled internally by the store. In v5 (Zustand), `setAccount` must be called explicitly via `refreshAccount()`.

### Fix

In `setupWebSocketTracking` inside `trackTransactions.ts`, after calling `recheckStatus()`, check whether there are no pending outgoing sessions. If so (incoming transaction case) and the user is logged in, call `refreshAccount()`.

**File:** `src/methods/trackTransactions/trackTransactions.ts`

```ts
const hasPendingSessions =
  Object.keys(
    pendingTransactionsSessionsSelector(store.getState())
  ).length > 0;

if (!hasPendingSessions && getIsLoggedIn()) {
  refreshAccount();
}
```

This is intentionally placed inside `setupWebSocketTracking` (WS event subscriber only) rather than in `checkTransactionStatus` or `recheckStatus`, to avoid triggering unnecessary API calls on:
- Initial `recheckStatus()` call at startup (line 81)
- Periodic polling interval (when WS is unavailable)

### Additional changes

None.

- [ ] Yes

author: m1ng112
body:
## Summary
- Ghostty 参考の Main + I/O スレッドモデルで全コンポーネントを統合
- Main Thread: winit イベントループ + wgpu レンダリング + カーソル点滅 (600ms)
- I/O Thread: tokio ランタイム + PTY read/write + VT パース (vte::Parser)
- crossbeam-channel (Main→I/O) + winit EventLoopProxy (I/O→Main) で通信
- Arc<Mutex<Terminal>> で端末状態を共有（ダーティフラグで描画最適化）
- キーボード入力を ANSI エスケープシーケンスに変換（矢印キー、F1-F12、Ctrl+キー対応）
- ウィンドウリサイズを GPU surface + Terminal grid + PTY に伝播
- Drop impl による安全なシャットダウン保証

Closes #9

## Changes
- **`src/event.rs`** (new): `IoEvent` / `WakeupReason` イベント型定義
- **`src/app.rs`** (rewrite): I/O スレッド生成、キーボードハンドリング、レンダーループ、リサイズ、シャットダウン
- **`src/main.rs`**: `EventLoop::with_user_event()` + `EventLoopProxy` 連携
- **`src/error.rs`**: `Pty` エラーバリアント追加
- **`Cargo.toml`**: `tokio`, `vte`, `wgpu` 依存追加

## Architecture
```
Main Thread                 I/O Thread
    |                           |
    |--- IoEvent::Input ------->|  (crossbeam-channel)
    |--- IoEvent::Resize ------>|
    |--- IoEvent::Shutdown ---->|
    |                           |
    |<-- WakeupReason ----------|  (winit EventLoopProxy)
    |   (TerminalUpdated,       |
    |    ChildExited)           |
    |                           |
    |--- Arc<Mutex<Terminal>> --|  (shared state)
```

author: kamibony
body:
This commit addresses two issues reported by the user:

1. **Empty Audio Transcription**: Mobile browsers (`web/public/mobile.html`) record audio in `.webm` format, while the OS client sends `.wav`. The backend was hardcoded to `audio/wav`, causing Gemini to silently fail parsing the WebM audio and return `EMPTY_AUDIO`. This is fixed by inspecting the magic bytes of the decoded Base64 audio stream to determine the correct MIME type.
2. **Silent Status Update Failure**: The user reported that the agent status was not updating correctly, despite no errors being thrown. To aid in debugging, explicit logging of the HTTP status code and response body has been added to the `firestore_update_document` function in `client/agent.py` right after the `session.patch()` call.

author: copilot
body:
Two separate issues addressed: (1) loading a plain-float checkpoint with `--quant_linear` (or a pre-quantized checkpoint without it) raised a state-dict key mismatch because `Int8Linear` was installed before `load_state_dict`, making `int8_weight`/`scale` keys conflict with checkpoint `weight` keys. (2) No graceful degradation existed when optional kernels (Flash Attention 3, SPARGE, Triton SLA) were unavailable.

## Key mismatch fix (`inference/modify_model.py`)

`create_model()` now auto-detects checkpoint format before mutating the model graph:

```python
checkpoint_is_quantized = any("int8_weight" in k for k in state_dict)

replace_linear_norm(net, replace_linear=checkpoint_is_quantized, ...)  # match checkpoint
net.load_state_dict(state_dict, assign=True)                            # never mismatches

if args.quant_linear and not checkpoint_is_quantized:
    replace_linear_norm(net, replace_linear=True, replace_norm=False, quantize=True)  # quantize after load
```

This makes `--quant_linear` at inference time equivalent in quality to pre-processing with `modify_model.py` (true INT8, not just structure installation).

## Attention fallback chain

### `rcm/utils/attention.py`
- Catches both `ModuleNotFoundError` and `ImportError` for `flash_attn_3`
- `deterministic=True` without FA3 now emits `UserWarning` instead of crashing
- `SDPBackend.MATH` appended to every `SDPA_BACKENDS` list
- SDPA call wrapped in `try/except RuntimeError` → hard-falls to `sdpa_kernel([MATH])` as final safety net

### `inference/modify_model.py` — `replace_attention()`
- No CUDA → skip replacement entirely, emit `UserWarning`, model runs on default SDPA
- `sagesla` + `SAGESLA_ENABLED=False` (missing `spas_sage_attn`) → fall back to `sla` with warning

### `SLA/core.py`
New `_sdpa_fallback()` helper (FA2 → cuDNN → efficient → MATH). Used in two fallback chains:

**SLA:** `Triton sparse kernel` → `RuntimeError` → `_sdpa_fallback()`

**SageSLA:** `SPARGE int8/fp8` → `RuntimeError` → `_attention.apply()` (SLA Triton, recomputes block map for BLKK=64 sm90 compat) → `RuntimeError` → `_sdpa_fallback()`

`return_sparsity` returns `1.0` when the SDPA path is taken (full attention = no sparsity applied).

author: rmolines
body:
## Summary

Adds [fractal](https://github.com/rmolines/fractal) to the **Plugins & Extensions** section.

**What it does:** Recursive project management for Claude Code. One primitive that decomposes any goal into verifiable predicates, works on the riskiest unknown first. The filesystem is the state — no database, no JSON.

**Key features:**
- `/fractal:run` — idempotent state machine, call repeatedly to advance the tree
- `/fractal:init` — bootstrap any goal into a predicate tree
- `/fractal:patch` — fast path for trivial leaf predicates
- Full sprint cycle: planning → delivery → review → ship
- Dry run mode — builds the full decomposition tree without executing
- Incremental decomposition with re-evaluation at each node

**Repo:** https://github.com/rmolines/fractal

## What is this contribution about?

NATS is now always available in local dev (via `ensureServices()`) and always present in production. This PR removes all non-NATS fallback implementations to simplify the codebase:

- **Deleted**: `PostgresNotifyStrategy`, `InMemoryToolListCache`, `InMemoryModelListCache`, `NoOpStreamBuffer`, `LocalCancelBroadcast`, and the `NOTIFY_STRATEGY` env var
- **Simplified**: `createEventBus()` always uses NATS notify + polling safety net; `app.ts` wiring always uses JetStream caches, `NatsCancelBroadcast`, `NatsStreamBuffer`
- **Kept**: `PollingStrategy` + `compose()` (required for scheduled/cron delivery), `LocalSSEBroadcast` (default for SSEHub before strategy is started, load-bearing for tests)
- **Net result**: -543 lines, +101 lines across 16 files

author: tobiasmcnulty
body:
This PR adds support for `--authurl`, an alternative to `--authfile` that delegates user authentication to an external HTTP service.

When a client connects, the server POSTs `{"username": "...", "password": "..."}` to the configured URL; a 200 response with a JSON array of address regexes grants access, while any other status denies it.

This approach works well in containerized environments where `--authfile` is limited by the lack of cross-container file-change notifications. The flag supports all existing address-matching functionality of `--authfile` and is mutually exclusive with it.

author: buffmcbighuge
body:
# Tempo Sync & Modulation

> Note: The additional "hello world" pipelines for tempo sync have been removed from this PR, they can still be found here: https://github.com/daydreamlive/scope/pull/672.

## Summary

Adds tempo synchronization and beat-synced parameter modulation to Scope. Pipelines can lock to Ableton Link or MIDI clock, quantize discrete parameter changes to beat boundaries, and continuously modulate parameters (e.g. `noise_scale`, `denoising_steps`) in sync with the beat. Target users are VDJs running Scope alongside Ableton Live, Resolume, or similar applications.

## What's in this PR

### Core

- **Tempo sync** — Ableton Link and MIDI clock support with optional dependencies (`aalink`, `mido`/`python-rtmidi`). When neither is installed, the UI shows install hints and the feature degrades gracefully.
- **Parameter scheduling** — Discrete parameter changes (prompt switches, denoising adjustments) can be quantized to beat/bar boundaries with configurable lookahead to compensate for pipeline latency.
- **Parameter modulation** — Continuous per-frame modulation of numeric parameters driven by beat phase. Pipeline-agnostic: operates on kwargs before they reach any pipeline.

### Frontend

- **Tempo Sync panel** — Source toggle (Link/MIDI), BPM input, beats per bar, live beat indicator, quantize mode, lookahead, beat cache reset rate, prompt cycle rate.
- **Modulation section** — Target selector (from schema `ui.modulatable` fields), wave shape (sine, cosine, triangle, saw, square, pulse decay), rate (½ beat → 4 bars), depth.
- **Prompt cycling** — Automatically advance through timeline prompts on beat/bar boundaries when enabled.

### Modulatable pipelines

LongLive, Krea, MemFlow, RewardForcing, StreamDiffusionV2 expose `denoising_steps` and (LongLive) `noise_scale` as modulatable via `ui_field_config(modulatable=True, ...)`.

---

## Architecture

```
Tempo Sources (Link / MIDI / Client-forwarded)
    → TempoSync Manager (BeatState, 15Hz notification loop)
    → ParameterScheduler (quantize discrete changes)
    → ModulationEngine (per-frame param modulation)
    → PipelineProcessor (inject beat state + modulated params)
    → Pipeline
```

- **Beat state:** `bpm`, `beat_phase`, `bar_position`, `beat_count`, `is_playing` injected into every pipeline call.
- **Cloud mode:** Browser forwards beat state over WebRTC data channel; server prefers client state when fresh (< 2s).
- **Modulation:** Config sent as `modulations` in parameter updates; Pydantic-validated on receipt.

---

## REST API

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| GET | `/api/v1/tempo/status` | Current tempo status and beat state |
| POST | `/api/v1/tempo/enable` | Enable tempo sync (Link or MIDI) |
| POST | `/api/v1/tempo/disable` | Disable tempo sync |
| POST | `/api/v1/tempo/set_tempo` | Set BPM (Link only) |
| GET | `/api/v1/tempo/sources` | Available tempo sources and capabilities |

**Modulation:** No dedicated REST API. Config is sent as `modulations` in WebRTC parameter updates.

---

## How to try it

1. **Install optional deps** (for Link or MIDI):
   ```bash
   uv sync --group link   # Ableton Link
   uv sync --group midi   # MIDI clock
   ```

2. **Run Scope** and start a stream.

3. **Open the Tempo Sync panel** in the sidebar. Enable tempo sync, choose Link or MIDI, set BPM.

4. **Quantize mode:** Set to "Beat" or "Bar" so changes like prompt switches land on the beat. Adjust lookahead if latency is visible.

5. **Modulation:** In the modulation section, pick a target (e.g. Noise Scale), choose shape/rate/depth, and toggle ON.

6. **Prompt cycling:** Add multiple prompts to the timeline, set `promptCycleRate` to "Bar" or "Beat", and prompts will advance automatically.

7. **Demo pipelines:** Use `metronome` to test lookahead or `mod-scope` to visualize modulation.

---

## Testing

- **ParameterScheduler:** `tests/test_parameter_scheduler.py` — adversarial tests for boundary math, concurrency, lookahead, and edge cases.
- **E2E:** Tests passed against fal.ai preview deployment.

---

## Optional dependencies

```toml
[project.optional-dependencies]
link = ["aalink>=0.1.1"]
midi = ["mido>=1.3.0", "python-rtmidi>=1.5.0"]
```

---

## Breaking changes

None. Tempo sync and modulation are additive. Pipelines that don't use beat kwargs are unaffected.

---

## Documentation

- `docs/tempo-sync-review.md` — Implementation review, architecture, API, edge cases, and future work.

---

  * Parameter scheduling aligned to beat boundaries with quantization modes
  * Beat-driven prompt cycling

* **Bug Fixes**

author: copilot
body:
Adds a second deduplication layer to `webhook_events` for cases where Asaas redelivers semantically identical payloads under a different `event_id`. The existing `UNIQUE(provider, event_id)` constraint handles same-ID redelivery; this adds `UNIQUE(provider, payload_hash)` (SHA-256 of the serialized payload) to catch content-identical duplicates.

## Schema
- `WebhookEvent` model: new `payload_hash String @db.Char(64)` field (after `payload`) + `@@unique([provider, payload_hash], map: "uq_webhook_provider_hash")`

## Migration (`20260317000000_add_webhook_payload_hash`)
- `ADD COLUMN payload_hash CHAR(64) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`
- Backfills via `encode(sha256(payload::text::bytea), 'hex')` (requires `pgcrypto`; migration runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto`)
- Drops the temporary default; creates the unique index

> Note: Postgres `payload::text` serialization differs from `JSON.stringify` — backfill is best-effort for dev/test rows only; all production rows receive the correct hash at insert time.

## Service (`webhookService.js`)
```js
function computePayloadHash(payload) {
  return createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify(payload)).digest('hex');
}
```
`findFirst` now queries with `OR: [{ event_id }, { payload_hash }]`. Both `create` and `update` (retry path) include `payload_hash`.

## Tests
New `describe('dedupe por payload_hash')`:
- Identical payload with different `event_id` → `{ skipped: true }`
- `payload_hash` present and hex-shaped (`/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/`) in the `create` call

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Task 04.2.2 — Dedupe por `event_id` / `payload_hash` em `webhook_events`

### Contexto

A tabela `webhook_events` já possui `UNIQUE(provider, event_id)` que protege contra redelivery do **mesmo evento** (mesmo `event_id`). Porém o Asaas pode ocasionalmente enviar dois eventos distintos com `event_id` diferentes mas **payload semanticamente idêntico** (duplicata por conteúdo). A task 04.2.2 adiciona uma segunda camada de dedupe: um hash SHA-256 do payload serializado (`payload_hash CHAR(64)`), com `UNIQUE(provider, payload_hash)`.

---

### Schema atual (`prisma/schema.prisma`) — modelo `WebhookEvent`

```prisma
/// Eventos de webhook recebidos de provedores externos. BIGSERIAL, hard-delete.
model WebhookEvent {
  id            BigInt    @id @default(autoincrement())
  provider      String    @db.VarChar(50)
  event_id      String    @db.VarChar(255)
  event_type    String    @db.VarChar(100)
  payload       Json      @db.JsonB
  processado    Boolean   @default(false)
  processado_em DateTime? @db.Timestamptz(6)
  erro          String?
  created_at    DateTime  @default(now()) @db.Timestamptz(6)

  @@unique([provider, event_id], map: "uq_webhook_provider_event")
  @@index([processado], map: "idx_webhook_processado")
  @@map("webhook_events")
}
```

---

## O que deve ser implementado

### 1. `prisma/schema.prisma` — adicionar campo `payload_hash`

Adicionar o campo `payload_hash` ao modelo `WebhookEvent`, **após o campo `erro`**, e uma segunda constraint unique:

```prisma
model WebhookEvent {
  id            BigInt    @id @default(autoincrement())
  provider      String    @db.VarChar(50)
  event_id      String    @db.VarChar(255)
  event_type    String    @db.VarChar(100)
  payload       Json      @db.JsonB
  payload_hash  String    @db.Char(64)
  processado    Boolean   @default(false)
  processado_em DateTime? @db.Timestamptz(6)
  erro          String?
  created_at    DateTime  @default(now()) @db.Timestamptz(6)

  @@unique([provider, event_id],       map: "uq_webhook_provider_event")
  @@unique([provider, payload_hash],   map: "uq_webhook_provider_hash")
  @@index([processado],                map: "idx_webhook_processado")
  @@map("webhook_events")
}
```

> **Posição do campo:** inserir `payload_hash` logo após `payload`, antes de `processado`.

### 2. Criar migration Prisma

Criar o arquivo `prisma/migrations/20260317000000_add_webhook_payload_hash/migration.sql` com o SQL necessário:

```sql
-- Migration: 04.2.2 — add payload_hash column and unique constraint to webhook_events
ALTER TABLE webhook_events
  ADD COLUMN payload_hash CHAR(64) NOT NULL DEFAULT '';

-- Backfill: set hash = encode(sha256(payload::text::bytea), 'hex') for existing rows
UPDATE webhook_events
   SET payload_hash = encode(sha256(payload::text::bytea), 'hex');

-- Remove the temporary default (column is NOT NULL, enforced going forward by app)
ALTER TABLE webhook_events
  ALTER COLUMN payload_hash DROP DEFAULT;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_webhook_provider_hash
  ON webhook_events (provider, payload_hash);
```

> **Nota:** O `encode(sha256(...))` usa `pgcrypto` ou a função nativa do Postgres 11+. Se o ambiente não tiver `pgcrypto`, usar `md5(payload::text)` como fallback para o backfill. Adicionar um comentário no SQL explicando.

### 3. `apps/api/src/services/webhookService.js` — calcular e persistir `payload_hash`

Ao criar ou atualizar o registro em `webhook_events`, sempre incluir `payload_hash` calculado como SHA-256 do JSON serializado do payload.

**Implementação:**

```js
import { createHash } from 'crypto';

/**
 * Calculates a SHA-256 hex digest of the given payload object.
 * Used as a secondary deduplication key in webhook_events.
 * @param {object} payload
 * @returns {string} 64-char hex string
 */
function computePayloadHash(payload) {
  return createHash('sha256')
    .update(JSON.stringify(payload))
    .digest('hex');
}
```

Depois, usar o hash na lógica de idempotência:

```js
// Em processarWebhookAsaas, ao verificar idempotência:
const payloadHash = computePayloadHash(payload);

const existing = await prisma.webhookEvent.findFirst({
  where: {
    provider: 'asaas',
    OR: [
      { event_id: String(payload.id) },
      { payload_hash: payloadHash },      // ← segunda camada de dedupe
    ],
  },
});

if (existing) {
  if (existing.processado) return { skipped: true };
  if (existing.erro === null) return { skipped: true };
  // falhou antes → permite retry
  await prisma.webhookEvent.update({
    where: { id: existing.id },
    data: { erro: null, payload, payload_hash: payloadHash },
  });
} else {
  await prisma.webhookEvent.create({
    data: {
      provider: 'asaas',
      event_id: String(payload.id),
      event_type: payload.event,
      payload,
      payload_hash: payloadHash,          // ← incluir no create
      processado: false,
    },
  });
}
```

### 4. `apps/api/src/services/__tests__/webhookService.test.js` — testes de dedupe por hash

Adicionar um `describe('dedupe por payload_hash')` co...

</details>

body:
## Summary
- **Bug fix**: Mollie sends multiple webhooks for the same resource ID on status transitions (e.g., `tr_abc123` for `authorized`, then again for `paid`). The unique index on `webhook_events.mollie_id` silently dropped subsequent webhooks, leaving payments stuck in intermediate states.
- Removed unique index on `webhook_events.mollie_id` — each webhook now creates a separate event row
- Added `RecordNotUnique` rescue to `Payment.record_from_mollie` and `Refund.record_from_mollie` (matching existing Subscription pattern) for concurrent INSERT race
- Added `discard_on ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` to `ProcessWebhookJob` to prevent retry amplification for unknown subscription/refund IDs
- Updated AGENTS.md, STYLE.md, README.md, tutorial, and CHANGELOG

## Migration Required
```sh
rails mollie_pay:install:migrations && rails db:migrate
```

## Testing
- Replaced 2 deduplication tests with 3 multi-event tests (same mollie_id creates separate events, enqueues separate jobs)
- Added RecordNotFound discard test for ProcessWebhookJob
- All 124 tests pass, zero rubocop offenses

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation
- **What to monitor**: `webhook_events` table growth rate, job queue depth, Mollie API error rate
- **Expected healthy behavior**: 2-3 webhook_events rows per payment lifecycle (vs 1 previously), all status transitions processed correctly
- **Failure signal**: Payments stuck in `authorized` status (same bug as before = rollback didn't work)
- **Validation**: `SELECT mollie_id, COUNT(*) FROM mollie_pay_webhook_events GROUP BY mollie_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` — non-zero results are now expected and normal

author: smileflow-steve
body:
This PR provides a comprehensive update to the SmileFlow Accessibility Widget, focusing on security, performance, and feature parity.

### Security Enhancements
- **XSS Protection:** Conducted a thorough audit of all dynamic DOM injections. Implemented a robust `escapeHTML` utility in `src/utils/escape.ts` and applied it to all user-controlled or dynamic data (e.g., button labels, keys, language options).
- **Dependency Updates:** Updated `esbuild`, `eslint`, and other dev dependencies to their latest secure versions. Switched from the deprecated `html-minifier` to `html-minifier-terser`.

### New Features
- **Accessibility Profiles:** Introduced predefined profiles (Visually Impaired, Dyslexia Friendly, Seizure Safe, High Contrast) that toggle multiple settings simultaneously for better UX.
- **Configurable Button Position:** Developers can now set the widget's position (e.g., `top-right`, `bottom-left`) and precise offsets via `pluginConfig`.
- **Custom Widget Icon:** Added support for passing custom SVG strings or image URLs in the configuration to override the default widget icon.
- **Revived Screen Reader:** Re-implemented the screen reader functionality using the native Web Speech API, allowing users to listen to element content on click.

### Optimization & Modernization
- **Bundler Refinement:** Updated `esbuild.config.js` to handle modern minification and ensure the final payload remains lightweight (~30kb).
- **Code Quality:** Resolved all 10+ ESLint errors and warnings. Replaced all legacy `@ts-ignore` directives with descriptive `@ts-expect-error` comments as per best practices.
- **Clean Up:** Removed dead code and simplified several tools (e.g., Screen Reader) for better maintainability.

### Verification
- **Linting:** `npm run lint` passes with zero errors/warnings.
- **Build:** `npm run build` successfully generates minified bundles for all formats (UMD, ESM, CJS).
- **Visual & Functional:** Verified through a comprehensive Playwright CUJ script, confirming that profiles correctly apply settings and the UI is responsive and properly sanitized.

## Overview

The plugin currently has **zero centralized CSS** — `assets/admin.css` is empty (0 bytes) and all styles are scattered as inline `style="..."` attributes across ~24 PHP files, plus `wp_add_inline_style()` blocks in the dashboard. This makes the UI inconsistent, hard to maintain, and **completely non-responsive on mobile devices**.

## Goals

1. **Populate `assets/admin.css`** with a complete design system
2. **Make ALL admin pages fully mobile-responsive** (phones, tablets, desktops)
3. **Replace inline styles** in PHP files with CSS classes
4. **Ensure `admin.css` is properly enqueued** via `wp_enqueue_style()` on all WBI admin pages
5. **Bump version to 8.0.0** in `wbi-suite.php` header

### CSS Variables (Custom Properties)
```css

    --wbi-shadow-md:  0 4px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.07);
    --wbi-font:       -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
```

### Component Classes
Create reusable classes for ALL modules to use:

- `.wbi-card` — Cards with subtle shadow, border-radius 12px, padding

- `.wbi-table` — Modern tables with hover, soft borders, sticky header

- `.wbi-alert` — Alert/notice styling

### Mobile-First Responsive Design (CRITICAL)

This is the most important requirement. ALL WBI admin pages must work perfectly on phones (320px+).

```css

/* Then progressive enhancement: */

@media (min-width: 600px)  { /* Tablets */ }
@media (min-width: 783px)  { /* WP admin breakpoint */ }
@media (min-width: 1024px) { /* Desktop */ }
```

author: isharryh
body:
## 概要

此 PR 对 MapTracker 若干代码进行了优化，尤其是：

1. 地图初始化的代码逻辑、代码可读性和执行效率。
2. 多尺度匹配算法的执行效率。

## Summary by Sourcery

将地图追踪（map-tracker）的资源加载与缩放逻辑集中到一个共享的资源管理器中，并调整大地图匹配参数，以提升性能和精度。

Bug 修复：
- 确保地图图像裁剪在保持确定性地图加载顺序的同时，正确遵守边界框（bounding boxes），并避免不必要的整型数组预计算。

增强改进：
- 使用全局的 `MapTrackerResource` 替代按推理（per-infer）的地图加载与缩放。该资源会按需惰性加载原始地图、按缩放因子缓存已缩放的变体，并在各个 map-tracker 组件之间共享这些资源。
- 优化 minicv 中的模板匹配工具，提供更清晰的 API、受控的并行度，以及优化后的多尺度搜索，以提升整体吞吐量。
- 调整大地图推理中的采样 padding、尺度搜索步长以及视口（viewport）计算逻辑，以提高定位的鲁棒性和效率。
- 简化大地图拾取（pick）动作处理逻辑，通过 switch 结构区分目标动作，并为大地图推理各阶段新增详细的耗时日志。

<details>
<summary>Original summary in English</summary>

## Summary by Sourcery

Centralize map-tracker resource loading and scaling into a shared resource manager, and tune big-map matching parameters for better performance and accuracy.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure map image cropping respects bounding boxes while maintaining deterministic map loading order and avoiding unnecessary integral array precomputation.

Enhancements:
- Replace per-infer map loading and scaling with a global MapTrackerResource that lazily loads raw maps, caches scaled variants by scale factor, and shares them across map-tracker components.
- Refine template matching utilities in minicv with clearer APIs, bounded parallelism, and optimized multi-scale search for improved throughput.
- Adjust big-map inference sampling paddings, scale search steps, and viewport computations to improve localization robustness and efficiency.
- Simplify big-map pick action handling by using a switch for target actions and add detailed timing logs for big-map inference phases.

</details>
